body: Interactive configuration of GSD workflow agents and model profile via multi-question prompt.
Routes to the settings workflow which handles:

- Interactive multi-question prompt covering model profile and workflow toggles (research, plan_check, verifier, drift guard, TDD, code review, worktrees, compact content, and more — see `gsd-core/workflows/settings.md` for the current set)
- Confirmation display with quick command references

Interactive configuration of GSD workflow agents (research, plan_check, verifier) and model profile selection via multi-question prompt. Updates the settings with user preferences. There are no global defaults here: the settings are this project's.
Read all files referenced by the invoking prompt's execution_context before starting.
Ensure config exists and load current state:
# the commands below are specforge commands: there is no launcher to define

# the settings live in specforge.json: there is no config path to resolve, and no active workstream (#2282).
if false; then   # there is no active-workstream file: the settings are one file, specforge.json

**If `response_language` is set:** All user-facing output of this workflow — narration between tool calls, status updates, progress notes, findings, questions, prompts, and explanations — MUST be presented in `{response_language}`. Technical terms, code, file paths, and subagent prompts stay in English — only user-facing output is translated.
Creates `config.json` (at the resolved path) with defaults if missing. `INIT` still holds `state.load` output for any step that needs STATE fields.
Store `$GSD_CONFIG_PATH` — all subsequent reads and writes use this path, not a hardcoded path, so active-workstream installs target the correct file (#2282).

end: These settings apply to future /gsd-plan-phase and /gsd-execute-phase runs.
- /gsd-config --integrations — configure API keys (Brave/Firecrawl/Exa), review.models CLI routing, and agent_skills injection
- /gsd-config --advanced — power-user tuning (plan bounce, timeouts, branch templates, cross-AI, context window, model policy)

- [ ] User presented with 25 settings (profile + workflow toggles + features + git branching + git tagging + ctx warnings + compact content), grouped into six sections: Planning, Execution, Docs & Output, Features, Model & Pipeline, Misc. `code_review_depth` is conditional on `code_review=on`. Model profile uses a two-question split (Q1: Adaptive / Standard tier / Inherit; Q2: Quality / Balanced / Budget — only when Standard tier chosen) to stay within the 4-option conversational prompting cap while exposing all 5 valid profiles (#3784). Drift Guard (`plan_review.source_grounding`) is in the Planning section.
- [ ] Config updated with model_profile, workflow, and git sections
- [ ] No global defaults written (there are none here)
In the shell blocks above, `$MILESTONE` is `v1.0` and `$PROJECT` is `taskboard`.

Every value is written with `specforge settings set @gsd/core <key> <value>` (the MCP tool `specforge.settings_set`), which checks the key and its type. The settings are the file `specforge.json`; there is no `config.json` and no workstream copy.

- A key another extension declares (`workflow.ui_*`, `workflow.code_review*`, `security_*`) is refused while that extension is not installed. Once it is, set it with its name: `specforge settings set @gsd/ui workflow.ui_phase false`.

- A search key (`brave_search`, `firecrawl`, `exa_search` and the others) is a secret: it is an environment variable, and `settings set` never writes it. `brave_search true|false` only forces the source on or off.
- `commit_docs`, `search_gitignored` and `graphify.*` are not settings here: the spec is source and is committed like code. Skip their questions.

## B. User Prompting
When the workflow needs user input, prompt the user conversationally:
- Present options as a numbered list in your response text
- Ask the user to reply with their choice
- For multi-select, ask for comma-separated numbers
## C. Tool Usage
Use these Cursor tools when executing GSD workflows:
- `Shell` for running commands (terminal operations)
- `StrReplace` for editing existing files
- `Read`, `Write`, `Glob`, `Grep`, `Task`, `WebSearch`, `WebFetch`, `TodoWrite` as needed
## D. Subagent Spawning
When the workflow needs to spawn a subagent:
- Use `Task(subagent_type="generalPurpose", ...)`
- The `model` parameter maps to Cursor's model options (e.g., "fast")

Check the spec with `specforge check`. Create and edit with `specforge new <kind> <id> ...`, `specforge set`,

## How to work
- **Computed is never written.** A status, a progress, a position and a count are computed from the graph. Where the
workflow says to update one, there is nothing to do.
- **Harness fields have one writer**: the command of `@gsd/core` that owns them (`specforge gsd <command>`; `specforge gsd help` lists them), never `specforge set`.
- **A command step's line has no arguments.** The step names the command; this text gives its arguments. Every
`--by` names who answers: `--by "<user>"` for a person, the agent's name for an agent.
- **Judges record their own verdicts** with `specforge gsd record-verdict` (the agent's body says how). An
orchestrator never records a verdict on a judge's behalf.
- **A refused call** (`gate_failed`, `human_only`, `stale_revision`, `invalid_input`) is reported to the user with its
message. Never edit the spec to get around it.
- **An agent this host does not have installed** (`gsd-debugger`, `gsd-ui-researcher`, `gsd-ui-checker`,
`gsd-code-reviewer`, `gsd-codebase-mapper`, ...) is skipped, and the skip is said.
- **Spawning an agent** on this host: as the adapter header above says (the agent is the installed `gsd-<name>`). The model is the installed agent's own: skip any model resolution.
- **References** the workflow names are read with `specforge gsd reference <path>`.
- **Ids in the shell blocks.** `$PHASE_ID` and `$PLAN_ID` are the entity the run is about (the end of this text names
it), `$MILESTONE` is the current milestone and `$PROJECT` the project (the end of this text names them too).
